Description: AI use has not meaningfully changed over the semester, or the reported change is minimal/vague. Apply when the student reports continuity, or a slight shift without substantive detail. Standalone.
Do NOT apply when: The student has never used AI at all (-> UC15). A specific, clear change is described (-> the relevant change code). A clear change is described that fits no code (-> UC13).
Distinguish from: UC15 (unchanged use vs. no use); UC13 (vague shift vs. clear-but-unclassifiable change)
Example responses: "no change really" • "Stayed consistent" • "slightly changed" • "I don't really use AI that much, so the way I've used it has stayed pretty consistent." • "Did not"

Description: Reported rise in how often AI is used, regardless of stated reason.
Do NOT apply when: The increase applies only in some contexts with decrease in others (-> UC04).
Example responses: "More frequent" • "As the subjects got harder i started using it more to get more understanding." • "Been using more" • "I use them more frequently to assist with outside work."

Description: Reported decline in how often AI is used, including stopping entirely after prior use. CO-CODE with UC12 when the student names a non-AI replacement resource, and with UC10 when the stated reason is distrust or discovered limitations.
Do NOT apply when: The student never used AI in the first place (-> UC15). Use varies by context rather than declining overall (-> UC04).
Distinguish from: UC15 (stopped vs. never started); UC04; UC12 and UC10 (co-occurring, not competing)
Example responses: "i have used them less than in the past" • "Stopped" • "I honestly use it less because I realized it's not that great at doing engineering." • "I've used them less overall mostly due to the environmental impact"

Description: Change in use that varies by subject, course, or problem difficulty rather than uniformly: more in some contexts, less in others.
Do NOT apply when: The change is uniform in one direction (-> UC02/UC03).
Example responses: "I use them much more frequently for math and physics but for mechanics I avoid it." • "AI works better for certain classes, and worse for others. I've only found it helpful in one class this semester, and it isn't mechanics."

Description: Student's use has moved TOWARD learning-support tasks: studying, flashcards, concept review, or deepening comprehension. Direction rule: Manner of Use codes (UC05-UC07) describe the manner the student has adopted or increased, never a manner they report abandoning.
Do NOT apply when: The student reports moving AWAY from concept support. The shift is toward checking their own completed work (-> UC07).
Distinguish from: UC07 (learning content vs. checking own work); UC09 (what AI is used for vs. deliberate self-restriction)
Example responses: "I use it more for studying now than anything else." • "I use it more now for concept learning/review" • "I've started to use AI for all my classes in learning, practicing, and doing things like flashcards."

Description: Student's use has moved TOWARD output generation: writing code, solving problems, or generating text for deliverables. Same direction rule as UC05.
Do NOT apply when: The student reports abandoning solution generation (usually -> UC09 or UC07 depending on what replaced it).
Example responses: "I will start to use it to generate experimental reports" • "I have learned to use it to help my code in certain classes and projects differently than before."

Description: Shift toward using AI to check or validate the student's own work rather than to generate it. Apply only when the student indicates doing the work themselves first. Same direction rule as UC05.
Do NOT apply when: The student asks AI to explain concepts from scratch (-> UC05). The change is a deliberate restriction to protect learning without a checking workflow (-> UC09; the two often co-occur).
Example responses: "I would rely less on it for completing problems and more just as a checking tool" • "I use AI more strategically now in order to check my homework." • "I use it more like a peer tutor (I check for its mistakes and it checks for mine) rather than just giving me answers"

Description: Improvement in how the student formulates queries or interacts with the tool: better prompting, providing more context, greater efficiency in getting useful responses.
Do NOT apply when: The change is which tool is used rather than how it is prompted (-> UC11).
Distinguish from: UC11; UC09 (better prompts vs. deliberately withholding information to protect learning)
Example responses: "Better at wording my questions to get the response I want" • "Trying to give it more context before asking any questions." • "Probably just efficiency and knowing how to ask questions better?"

Description: Deliberate moderation or restriction of AI to protect one's own learning: expressed concern about over-reliance, or intentionally limiting the task (e.g., withholding numbers) so the student still does the cognitive work.
Do NOT apply when: The reduction is driven by AI's unreliability rather than by protecting one's own learning (-> UC10, often with UC03).
Distinguish from: UC10 (protecting own learning vs. distrusting the tool); UC03
Example responses: "I tried not to use AI while learning the material and practicing proble[ms]" • "I am just making sure that I don't rely too much on AI to help me solve problems." • "now I try to give it the structure of the problem without numebrs so I still have to do the work myself"

Description: Growth in critical evaluation and awareness of AI limitations: questioning outputs, discovering poor performance in specific domains (e.g., trusses, diagrams), no longer trusting implicitly.
Do NOT apply when: The motivation is protecting one's own learning rather than the tool's reliability (-> UC09).
Example responses: "I started to question the answers a lot more as I went through the semester." • "Less accurate for trusses" • "being cautious when AI has to interpret graphs and stuff like that" • "I am more skeptical, but overall it hasn't changed very much." (co-code UC10 + UC01? No: a stance change IS a change; code UC10 alone)

Description: Change in the AI tool, platform, or tier used: switching primary tools, using different models for different purposes, or changing subscription tiers.
Do NOT apply when: The change is in prompting technique with the same tool (-> UC08).
Example responses: "I was using ChatGPT at the beginning, then switched to Claude around March." • "Now I use different platforms for different uses." • "i bought pro plan" • "I have started using other models rather than sticking to one."

Description: Shift toward non-AI learning resources: instructors, office hours, TAs, textbooks, lecture notes, or videos in place of AI. Usually co-occurs with UC03.
Do NOT apply when: No specific non-AI replacement is named (UC03 alone).
Distinguish from: UC03 (co-occurring: UC03 = less AI, UC12 = named replacement)
Example responses: "I've used it less and pivoted to office hours and youtube videos" • "I relied on it a little less because I preferred looking over lecture notes" • "students would be better off going to instructors with doubts"

Description: A valid, CLEAR change in AI use that fits none of the themes above and is too idiosyncratic to warrant its own code. Describe the change in the notes field.
Do NOT apply when: The change is vague or minimal (-> UC01). Any other code fits, even at low confidence (apply it and flag instead).
Example responses: "Can pace myself better." • "I use ai where I would have searched the answer"

Description: Responses that are blank, nonsensical, or fail to address the prompt about changes in AI use in any capacity. Standalone.
Do NOT apply when: Any other code can be applied, even at low confidence (apply it and flag instead). "None"/"No changes" address the prompt (-> UC01).
Distinguish from: UC01 (a no-change answer is codable, not noise)
Example responses: "Na" • "N/A" • "I knew most of the material covered." (does not address the prompt)

Description: Student states they do not use AI at all and have not during the semester, so the change question does not apply. Standalone.
Do NOT apply when: The student used AI and reduced or stopped (-> UC03). The student uses AI rarely but consistently (-> UC01).
Example responses: "I didn't use AI" • "None, still haven't used it"
